passage:
Monday
Joseph put a little clay elephant on my desk before first period. He painted it himself. Then he kept looking back at me all through Hindi, and I couldn't concentrate.
It was sweet, but I felt uncomfortable. I don't like him that way.
At break I gave it back. "Thank you, Joseph, it's really nice. But I'm not comfortable keeping it. Can we just be classmates?"
He went pink and said okay.
But after lunch there was a note in my bag: "Please keep it." I showed Ms Rao. She said I'd been clear and kind, and she'd have a quiet word with Joseph today. She did, before home time.
Gargi

qa.q: What did Joseph put on Gargi's desk?
qa.a: A little clay elephant he painted himself.

qa.q: How did Gargi feel about the gift and Joseph looking back?
qa.a: Gargi felt uncomfortable and distracted, even though the gift was sweet.

qa.q: What did Gargi do that was clear and kind?
qa.a: Gargi returned the gift politely with thanks, and when Joseph kept pushing with a note, told Ms Rao, who spoke to him that day.

qa.q: How might Joseph have felt when the gift came back?
qa.a: Joseph was likely embarrassed and disappointed, going pink.

grounding: A boy gives Gargi a gift and keeps looking; Gargi says a polite no and, when he keeps pushing, tells a trusted adult who acts.

passage:
At the village fair, Irfan came up to Shabnam and held out a glass bangle. "For you," he said, and grinned. All evening he kept turning up wherever she was: at the swings, the sweet stall, the puppet show.
Shabnam's cheeks felt hot. She didn't want the bangle, and she didn't like him following her.
She held it out. "Thank you, Irfan, but no. Please give it to your sister."
Irfan's face fell. But ten minutes later he was behind her again.
Shabnam found her uncle Yogesh at the tea stall and told him. Yogesh Chacha walked over to Irfan and said calmly, "She said no. Leave her be now." Irfan went off to his friends.

qa.q: What did Irfan offer Shabnam?
qa.a: A glass bangle.

qa.q: How did Shabnam feel when Irfan kept turning up?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable and embarrassed, with hot cheeks, not liking being followed.

qa.q: What did Shabnam do that was right?
qa.a: She said a polite, clear no and, when Irfan kept following, told her uncle Yogesh, who stepped in.

qa.q: How might Yogesh Chacha see Irfan's behaviour?
qa.a: Yogesh Chacha sees that Irfan isn't listening to Shabnam's no, so he calmly tells him to leave her be.

grounding: A boy gives a girl a small gift and keeps following her; she says a polite no, and when he keeps pushing she tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Wednesday
Today Kamal told me a secret behind the library. He wants to join the kathak class, but he's scared his cousins will laugh. "You're the only one who knows," he said.
I felt special. Also like I was holding something that could break.
At lunch Sonam asked why Kamal was so quiet. I just said, "Dunno."
I've decided: I'll keep it. It's his to tell. If it were something that could hurt him, like someone being mean to him at home, I'd tell a teacher and explain to him why. But this is just his dream.
Maybe I'll go with him to watch the class.
Tenzin

qa.q: Which class does Kamal want to join?
qa.a: The kathak class.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel when Kamal shared the secret?
qa.a: Tenzin felt special and trusted, but also responsible, as if holding something that could break.

qa.q: When would Tenzin tell an adult instead of keeping the secret?
qa.a: If the secret meant Kamal could be hurt, Tenzin would tell a teacher and explain why.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel knowing Tenzin kept his secret?
qa.a: Kamal would likely feel safe and trust Tenzin more.

grounding: A friend shares a secret and Tenzin feels special and responsible, keeping it because no one could be hurt.

passage:
On the way back from school, Pankaj whispered to Reena, "Promise not to tell? Tonight after dinner I'm going to swim across the canal. The big boys dared me. It's full because of the rain."
Reena felt a rush of pride that he trusted her. Then a cold feeling. The canal was fast and brown after the rain.
"Pankaj, that's dangerous. I can't keep this one."
"You promised!"
"I know. But you could drown. I'm sorry."
At home she told her mother straight away. Her mother walked to Pankaj's house before dinner and spoke to his father. Pankaj stayed home.
Next day Reena told him, "I told because I care. Not to get you in trouble."

qa.q: Why was the canal full?
qa.a: Because of the rain.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Reena have when Pankaj told her?
qa.a: She felt proud he trusted her, then scared, because the canal was fast and dangerous.

qa.q: Why was Reena right to break her promise?
qa.a: Pankaj could have been badly hurt, so telling a trusted adult was the caring choice, and she explained why to him.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel when Reena explains why she told?
qa.a: Pankaj may feel angry at first, but might also see that she did it because she cares.

grounding: A friend tells a girl a secret; she feels trusted but, because he could be hurt, she tells a trusted adult the same day and explains why.

passage:
Hostel warden's note, Thursday.
Jatin confided in Nilesh this week that his family is moving to another city at the end of term. He asked Nilesh not to tell anyone yet.
Tonight I heard Nilesh in the corridor, whispering, "I know something big about Jatin..." to another boy. He stopped halfway, then said, "Never mind."
Later, Nilesh came to me, looking troubled. He said he'd almost told, and had actually told one boy yesterday. I suggested he own up. He went to Jatin straight away and apologised. Jatin was upset, but they talked for a long time. I'll keep an eye on both boys.

qa.q: What secret did Jatin share with Nilesh?
qa.a: That his family is moving to another city at the end of term.

qa.q: How was Nilesh feeling when he came to the warden?
qa.a: Nilesh looked troubled and guilty about almost telling and having told one boy.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do after he slipped?
qa.a: He owned up to Jatin and apologised instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Jatin feel when Nilesh apologises?
qa.a: Jatin was upset that his secret got out, but Nilesh's honesty let them talk it through.

grounding: A boy is tempted to share a friend's big secret, slips once, then owns up and apologises, showing trust is fragile.

passage:
Saturday
Baljeet told me the BIGGEST secret today. Her family is adopting a baby girl next month! She said, "Don't tell anyone yet. Mama wants to wait until the papers are done."
I was bursting all afternoon. At tuition, Rinku asked, "Why are you smiling?" and the words were right there on my tongue.
But I thought about how Baljeet looked when she told me, so happy and so worried. If I told, I couldn't take it back.
So I said, "Nothing. Just a good day."
It was SO hard. But I feel proud now, like I'm someone who can be trusted.
Vasudha

qa.q: What is Baljeet's family doing next month?
qa.a: Adopting a baby girl.

qa.q: How did Vasudha feel when Rinku asked about the smile?
qa.a: Vasudha felt bursting with excitement and tempted to tell.

qa.q: What helped Vasudha keep the secret?
qa.a: Remembering how happy and worried Baljeet looked, and knowing a told secret cannot be taken back.

qa.q: How might Baljeet feel if she knew Vasudha kept it?
qa.a: Baljeet would feel relieved and trust Vasudha even more.

grounding: Vasudha is desperate to share a friend's exciting secret but remembers trust is fragile and keeps it.

passage:
Wasim had told only Elizabeth that he was scared of dogs, even little ones. Now, in the colony park, Karan barked right behind him and everyone laughed. "Woof! Run, Wasim!"
Wasim's face went hot. Elizabeth was standing right there, looking at her shoes.
He could tell everyone her secret, that she still sucked her thumb when she slept. He wanted to.
Instead, after the others left, he walked over. "I told you that because I trusted you. It really hurt."
Elizabeth's eyes filled. "I'm sorry. It just slipped out."
"Okay," Wasim said. "But I'll be careful what I tell you for a while."

qa.q: What was Wasim scared of?
qa.a: Dogs, even little ones.

qa.q: How did Wasim feel when Karan barked behind him?
qa.a: He felt hurt and embarrassed, his face going hot.

qa.q: What did Wasim do that was wise?
qa.a: He told Elizabeth calmly how it felt instead of revealing her secret back, and decided to be careful with trust for a while.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth feel after Wasim spoke to her?
qa.a: Elizabeth felt sorry and ashamed, with her eyes filling.

grounding: A boy's best friend spreads his secret; he feels hurt, tells her how it felt instead of being cruel back, and decides to trust her carefully for a while.

passage:
"Uma, can I talk to you?"
"Sure, Samir."
"Everyone in class knows I'm going to a speech therapist. Only you knew."
Uma bit her lip. "I told Radha. I didn't think she'd tell anyone."
"It felt horrible. Like everyone was staring at me."
"I'm really sorry."
"I trusted you."
"I know. I messed up."
Samir was quiet. He could say something mean about her. He knew things too. But he didn't want to be like that.
"I'm going to be careful what I tell you for a while."

qa.q: How did Samir feel when everyone knew?

qa.q: What did Samir do that showed maturity?
qa.a: He told Uma how it felt and chose to be careful with trust rather than hurting her back.

qa.q: How might Uma feel after the conversation?
qa.a: Uma seems sorry and determined to earn back Samir's trust.

grounding: A boy's best friend shares his secret; he tells her how it felt, chooses not to be cruel back, and decides to trust her carefully for now.

passage:
Tuesday night
Today at break Nandini showed me the marks on her arm and whispered that someone at home hurts her when they're angry. She made me promise not to tell.
My stomach felt sick all through maths. I love Nandini. I didn't want to break a promise. But this felt way too big for me.
After school I went to Ms Pereira and told her. She listened carefully and said, "You did the right thing. This isn't your fault or Nandini's." She took me to the counsellor straight away, and they called Nandini in before she went home.
Later I told Nandini, "I told because I care about you. You shouldn't have to be hurt."
She cried, but she hugged me.
Kamal

qa.q: What did Nandini show Kamal at break?
qa.a: The marks on her arm.

qa.q: How did Kamal feel after hearing Nandini's secret?
qa.a: Kamal felt sick and torn, loving Nandini and not wanting to break a promise, but knowing it was too big to carry alone.

qa.q: Why was telling Ms Pereira the right choice?
qa.a: Nandini was being hurt, and Ms Pereira acted that same day by taking Kamal to the counsellor and calling Nandini in before she went home.

qa.q: How might Nandini feel when Kamal explains why he told?
qa.a: Nandini seemed upset but also comforted, crying and then hugging Kamal.

grounding: A friend tells Kamal she is being hurt at home; Kamal tells a teacher the same day, who acts with the counsellor, and Kamal gently explains to her that telling is loving.

passage:
Behind the village school, Avni pulled her sleeve down fast. "Don't tell anyone, Jahnavi. My uncle gets angry and hits me. If I tell, it'll be worse."
Jahnavi's heart pounded. She wanted to keep her friend's secret. But this was too big.
"Avni, I can't keep this one. You shouldn't be hurt."
Avni started crying. "Please don't."
Jahnavi held her hand. "Let's go to Headmistress Ma'am together. Right now."
Avni was scared, but she came.
The headmistress listened without interrupting. She sat with Avni and said, "This is not your fault. You were brave to come." Before school ended, she called the child helpline and arranged for Avni to be safe that night.

qa.q: Who did Avni say hits her?
qa.a: Her uncle.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi feel when Avni told her?
qa.a: She felt shocked and scared, her heart pounding, knowing the secret was too big to keep.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi do that was loving, not disloyal?
qa.a: She told Avni gently that she couldn't keep it, then went with her straight to the headmistress.

qa.q: How might the headmistress see her role?
qa.a: The headmistress sees that Avni must be protected, so she stays with her, reassures her and calls the helpline that same day.

grounding: A friend confides that she is being hurt at home; the girl gently explains she cannot keep it and they tell the headmistress, who acts the same day.

passage:
The school bus was stuck in traffic for an hour, and everyone was hot and cranky. Shreya and Nikita were arguing about the window seat. Then Nikita snapped, "At least I don't still sleep with a teddy bear, Shreya!"
The whole bus laughed. Shreya went scarlet and turned to the window.
Nikita's stomach dropped. That was the secret Shreya had told her in Class 3.
When the bus finally reached school, Nikita caught up with her. "I'm really sorry. There's no excuse. I was angry, but that's my fault, not yours."
Shreya didn't look at her. "I need some time."
"Okay. I'll wait."

qa.q: What secret did Nikita shout on the bus?
qa.a: That Shreya still sleeps with a teddy bear.

qa.q: How did Nikita feel after she let the secret out?
qa.a: She felt awful and guilty, her stomach dropping.

qa.q: What did Nikita do right in her apology?
qa.a: She said sorry with no excuses, took responsibility and accepted that Shreya needed time.

qa.q: How might Shreya feel after Nikita apologises?
qa.a: Shreya is still hurt and embarrassed, needing time before trusting Nikita again.

grounding: A girl lets out her friend's secret in a fight and feels awful; she apologises without excuses and accepts trust will take time.

passage:
In the Chennai school canteen, Anjali and Lavanya argued over a group project. Anjali's voice rose. "Well, at least I didn't fail maths last term, Lavanya!"
The table went silent. Lavanya's face crumpled. Only Anjali had known.
Anjali felt sick. She wanted to say Lavanya had made her angry. But that was just an excuse.
After lunch she found Lavanya by the lockers. "I'm sorry. That was your secret, and I used it to hurt you. It was completely my fault."
Lavanya wiped her eyes. "I trusted you."
"I know. I'll understand if you need time."
Lavanya nodded slowly.

qa.q: How did Anjali feel after revealing the secret?

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel after Anjali's apology?
qa.a: Lavanya is still hurt but may begin to trust again because Anjali took full responsibility.

grounding: A girl reveals her friend's secret in a fight and feels awful; she apologises without excuses and accepts trust will take time.

passage:
In the school counsellor's room, Sachin twisted his tie. "I lost the tablet the school lent me. Two weeks ago. I haven't told Papa."
Mr Joseph, the counsellor, nodded. "What are you afraid of?"
"That he'll shout. That he'll be really angry."
"Some things are okay to keep private. But a big worry like this is heavy. What if you start with, 'Papa, there's something I have to say. Please don't shout'?"
Sachin practised it twice.
At pick-up, in the school car park, he said it. Papa's face tightened for a second. Then he said, "Thank you for telling me. We'll sort it out together."
Sachin felt lighter than he had in two weeks.

qa.q: What had Sachin lost?
qa.a: The tablet the school lent him.

qa.q: What was Sachin afraid of?
qa.a: He was afraid Papa would shout and be really angry.

qa.q: How did Mr Joseph help Sachin share the worry?
qa.a: He explained that big worries need sharing and helped Sachin practise starting with "Papa, there's something I have to say. Please don't shout."

qa.q: How might Papa have felt hearing the news?
qa.a: Papa was briefly upset, but stayed calm and thanked Sachin, wanting to sort it out together.

grounding: A boy hides a big worry from his father out of fear; a counsellor helps him start with a gentle opening, and his father reacts calmly.

Monday. Alka leaned over. "If you tell me what Meher said about her parents, I'll let you sit with us at lunch."
Zainab's stomach dropped. She had been eating alone all week. "No," she said.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Monday. Vinita.
Hrithik (Class 5) came to me at lunch, very quiet. He said a man who helps at his after-school tuition has been giving him chocolates and saying, "This is our secret. Don't tell your parents." Hrithik said it made his tummy feel funny.
I stayed with him and listened. I told him it was never his fault, and that telling me was brave and right. He looked relieved.
I phoned his mother at once and she came to school within the hour. I also informed the principal, who is contacting the tuition centre and the proper authorities today. Hrithik will not attend tuition until this is sorted.

qa.q: How did Hrithik feel about the secret?
qa.a: He felt uneasy, saying it made his tummy feel funny.

qa.q: What did Vinita do after Hrithik told?
qa.a: Vinita stayed with him, said it wasn't his fault, praised his bravery, called his mother at once and informed the principal the same day.

qa.q: How might Hrithik's mother feel when she hears?
qa.a: She would likely feel worried and protective, coming to school within the hour.

grounding: An older person tells a boy to keep a secret from his parents; the boy tells a trusted adult, who says it is not his fault and acts the same day.

passage:
Wednesday
